$comment: Contract for workspace/reports/security_props.json, written by scripts/security_props.py run (plan step I9): the MetAcsl security properties the threat model requires (L4-L6), the frame obligations (L3), and the ledger obligations per function (`file#name`).

function_id.$comment: A function id, `file#name`: the file relative to the target root (any character but `#`), then one symbol name. The name may carry what nm prints for a compiler clone or a versioned symbol (`parse.constprop.0`, `f@@VERS_1`).

site.$comment: a call site in a function: `callee` called at `line` of the function's file

at.$comment: where the check goes: before the declaration that holds the call, or after it

check.$comment: the annotation written into the work tree; `${argN}` stands for the text of the call's N-th argument (0-based)

decl.$comment: where its first declaration is, when the model knows

stub.$comment: workspace/stubs/<header>:<line>: the contract was read in the run's stub overlay (a filled or hand-written stub, which Frama-C finds before the real header), not at `decl`

assigns.$comment: the assigns terms read in that contract (`stub`, else `decl`)

preamble.$comment: ACSL every meta file starts with (templates/metacsl/preamble.acsl)

variant.$comment: the template variant of an asset, invariant or call-rule property (templates/metacsl/l3_asset.acsl, l4_invariant.acsl, l4_call_rule.acsl)

engines.$comment: present when not every engine of `meta_engines` may load the property: the ones that may (WP always does). A monotonic invariant lists `eacsl` only: Eva does not evaluate \at(x, Before). security_props.for_engine filters on it

init_checks.$comment: package E: the calls placed in initializers (`int n = f(x);`) in the property's instances, where MetAcsl 0.12 generates no instance of its context. `run` writes each `check`, named after the property, into the work tree (`code_checks` lists the ones placed). A site whose check could not be written moves to `unchecked`

unchecked.$comment: what the property does not check although its targets hold it: an initializer call no check could be written for (`callee`, `line`), or a function left out of the targets (a callee whose `assigns` would stop MetAcsl). The ledger must not credit the function's unit of this property's class from a run without a goal

declared_callees.$comment: a \writing property (asset writers, auth state, monotonic invariant) takes what a declared callee writes from its `assigns`. Per property, the declared functions its targets call: `set_assigns` (an `assigns` holding \union(...) or {a, b}, which stops MetAcsl: their callers are left out of the targets and listed under `unchecked`), `no_assigns` (no `assigns` in the contract: the stub overlay's when it stubs the function, else the first declaration's; MetAcsl generates nothing for what they write, silently), `unknown` (the declaration could not be read)

acsl.$comment: the meta-property annotation(s), ready to parse

instances.$comment: functions whose WP proof holds the generated annotations: the ledger units

sources.$comment: files defining the globals the property names, parsed with every WP run that loads it

threat_model.$comment: the threat-model item the property comes from

decided.$comment: instances decided from the model instead of by a WP goal (plan step M2): not in `instances`, recorded by the ledger seed

taint.$comment: where the work tree gets Eva taint annotations for this secret (plan step M3, `run --eva-taint`)

args.$comment: [pointer argument index, length argument index or null]

code.$comment: a property written into the work tree, not into the meta file: a local secret's wipe `check` (plan step M6, `local`), an auth gate's failure `check` before each return (M7, `returns`; `${result}` stands for the returned expression), or a wrapper sink's `check` before each call that hands its buffer on (`handoff`; `${predicate}` stands for `bytes` or `object` on that call's arguments)

handoff.$comment: the calls to check before, in the wrapper: `callee` is the called name (a function, or with `member` the field or pointer the call goes through), `args` the [pointer argument index, length argument index or null] pairs to check, `sites` how many such calls the model records (null: unknown)

relocated.$comment: a wrapper sink (threat model `checked_at`): the property is not generated at the wrapper's callers but checked inside the wrapper, before each call that hands the buffer to an inner sink

not_generated_at.$comment: the wrapper's callers, which no longer hold an instance

checked_at.$comment: each call in the wrapper the check is written before; an indirect call lists every function the model says it can dispatch to (the check does not depend on which one)

superseded.$comment: instances of the inner sinks' own properties in the wrapper that the check replaces: MetAcsl cannot state them at a call through a pointer

other_indirect_calls.$comment: the wrapper's other calls through a pointer (a hook that completes the buffer): not checked

forwarded_to.$comment: a forwarding sink (L5): a bytes sink the target defines that reaches these declared bytes sinks in the model's call graph. Its bytes are checked at their calls, where they leave; the property has no instance and no MetAcsl text (`acsl` is a comment)

decided.$comment: decided from the model, no WP goal (plan step M2)

unchecked.$comment: the function is held by the property but left out of its targets (a callee whose `assigns` stops MetAcsl): why. No WP run has a goal for it, and none may credit the unit

code_checks.$comment: plan step M6: each in-code check placed in the work tree (file, line: where Eva reports its status)

index.$comment: package E, a check at an initializer call: its 0-based position among the generated checks of that line, in source order. A Frama-C report gives a check's file and line but not its name, and one declaration can carry the checks of several properties

eva_taint.$comment: the Eva taint annotations written into the work tree (plan step M3); absent from reports older than it

checks.$comment: each taint check placed: where Eva reports its status (ledger.py ingest-eva names the property from it)

modules.$comment: harness modules whose EVA_TAINT this run set

meta_engines.$comment: the engines that check the MetAcsl properties besides WP (run --meta-engines, sticky): eva loads them in each harness module's Phase 2 run, eacsl compiles them into the Phase 1 fuzz build; absent or empty: WP only

initializer_flags.$comment: whether the Phase 0 model says which calls are placed in an initializer (`call_sites[].initializer`, dump schema 5). MetAcsl 0.12 generates no \calling, \writing (from the callee's `assigns`) or \strong_invariant instance at such a call. `known` false: `properties` lists the properties of those contexts, and ledger.py refuses them the no-goal credit (`wp_meta_initializers_unknown`). Absent from a document older than this field: the ledger refuses that credit to every MetAcsl unit until `security_props.py run` writes it
